svg.aria-label: Where the Zmod ADC fits: a Zmod Scope pod on a SYZYGY port is wired to the programmable logic, where a bitstream provides the ADC controller and an AXI DMA; AXI and interrupts connect them to the processing system and Linux. The order of work is: boot the PS first, build a PL design, load its bitstream before the kernel probes it, add device-tree nodes, then a driver.
svg.text: Where the Zmod ADC fits: PS boots first, then a PL design, then a driver
The Zmod connectors are wired to the FPGA fabric, not to the processors. Nothing about them works until a bitstream and a driver exist. This is a map, not a build.
THE HARDWARE PATH OF A SAMPLE
plugged into port A or B
wired to the PL, one I/O bank
each; VADJ set by the platform
MCU after it reads the pod's DNA
The amber stages do not exist until steps 2 and 3 below. The PS side (UART, SD, Ethernet) is untouched by any of this: it is why the first boot needs no bitstream.
Do this first and keep it as the
PS preset of the board + Digilent's
Zmod ADC IP + AXI DMA; export a
the PL nodes: U-Boot, or an FSBL-style
Nodes for the DMA engine and the ADC
at the addresses of step 2: static
an IIO driver for the ADC controller,
Then read samples from user space.
the one piece nobody ships in mainline
Why this order: a node whose hardware is not configured makes Linux hang on its first register access, so the bitstream must be in the fabric before the driver probes.
And a Zmod pod is not hot-swappable: power the board off before you plug or unplug one (reference manual, section 8).
Facts: Eclypse Z7 reference manual (Zmod ports, SmartVIO, I2C), Digilent's Eclypse-Z7-OS project (Zmod ADC design, DMA via xilinx_axidma and UIO), UG585 (PS-PL interfaces).
A bench-proven configuration drives the Zmod Scope with xilinx_dma plus a small IIO driver, one DMA channel per ADC, and loads the bitstream through the kernel's FPGA manager after boot.
